rounds.text: FlySBS Aviation Ltd is profoundly under-appreciated, trading at a modest P/E of 13.3x [E1] despite phenomenal compounding power, with 5-year sales and profit growth surging at 82% and 109% respectively [E14, E17]. This top and bottom-line velocity is backed by elite capital efficiency, featuring a 5-year median ROE of 27% [E20] and a sector-crushing ROCE of 32.5% [E12] compared to a paltry sector median of just 7.1% [E58]. The business is generating real economic value, printing Rs 32 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 29 Cr in free cash flow for Mar 2026 [E27, E28], all while maintaining a conservatively financed balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of only 0.12x [E30]. Furthermore, working capital discipline has materially improved, with operational cycles shortening from 51.4 days to 32.7 days [E44], and the broader services sector provides a supportive macroeconomic tailwind with a score of +0.57 [E54, E55]. A reverse DCF indicates the current market price of ₹ 469 implies a meager 2.6% earnings growth rate [E39], completely ignoring a fundamental growth trajectory that has recently expanded operating margins by 8 percentage points to 22% [E23]. Conceded: [E4], [E26], [E36], [E45], [E46], [E47].

Despite reported profitability, the company exhibits a concerning gap between earnings and actual cash generation, with a cash conversion ratio of just 0.52x and operating cash flow representing only 60% of operating profit in March 2026 [E26, E29]. This disconnect is compounded by deteriorating working capital metrics as debtor days have stretched from 35.2 to 43.8 days [E47], while borrowings have sharply doubled from Rs 18 Cr to Rs 37 Cr within a single year [E31]. Institutional confidence is visibly eroding, highlighted by a negative money flow signal driven by foreign institutions cutting their stake to 2.01% and domestic institutions slashing theirs to 0.66% [E34, E35, E36]. Furthermore, governance and shareholder alignment are questionable given the low promoter holding of 32.5% [E46] and a complete refusal to distribute any of the reported earnings to shareholders, resulting in a 0.00% dividend yield [E4, E45]. Compounding these operational and structural red flags, operating margins demonstrate an inconsistent trend both yearly and quarterly over the short term [E24, E25]. Conceded: the business displays strong multi-year compounded sales and profit growth alongside high historical return metrics [E14, E17, E43].

The bear highlights a cash conversion ratio of 0.52x and operating cash flow at 60% of operating profit [E26, E29], but this still translates to a very substantial Rs 32 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 29 Cr in free cash flow [E27, E28]. Conceded: debtor days have stretched to 43.8 days and borrowings have increased to Rs 37 Cr [E31, E47], yet the debt-to-equity ratio remains at a very conservative 0.12x [E30]. Conceded: institutional holdings and dividend yields are low or decreasing [E4, E34, E35, E46], but this overlooks stellar fundamental execution, including a 32.5% ROCE, a 26.2% ROE, and multi-year sales and profit growth exceeding 100% [E12, E13, E18, E19]. Conceded: operating margins show an inconsistent short-term trend [E24, E25], but the broader picture reveals operating margin expanding by 8 percentage points over three years to reach 22% [E23]. Finally, working capital requirements have actually improved overall, with the cycle dropping from 51.4 days down to 32.7 days [E44].

Conceded: multi-year sales and profit growth sit at high levels [E15, E18], and ROCE reaches 32.5% [E12]. However, the bull glosses over the severe quality issues hidden behind those reported earnings, specifically a cash conversion ratio of just 0.52x where profits run far ahead of actual cash generation, pointing to mounting accruals [E26]. Conceded: the debt-to-equity ratio sits at a conservative 0.12x [E30], yet actual borrowings doubled year-over-year from Rs 18 Cr to Rs 37 Cr [E31], matching a sharp rise in debtor days from 35.2 to 43.8 days [E47]. Conceded: the multi-year operating margin expanded to 22% [E23], but this progress is undercut by an inconsistent short-term yearly and quarterly margin trend [E24, E25] alongside a complete zero dividend yield [E4]. Most damningly, smart money is fleeing the stock, evidenced by domestic institutions slashing their stake from 3.21% to 0.66%, foreign investors trimming holdings, and scanX flagging negative institutional money flow [E34, E35, E36].
